prompt: A Deployment rollout stalls. Old Pods are Ready; new Pods restart with OOMKilled and sometimes fail readiness. HPA requests more replicas, but some remain Pending. Lead diagnosis and recovery.
directAnswer: Freeze rollout/scaling edits and state user impact. Bind Deployment UID/generation, old/new ReplicaSet revisions and Pod UIDs. Preserve new Pod lastState, previous logs, events, memory/request/limit metrics and readiness results. nodeName separates the OOM/readiness Pods from Pending placement failures. Compare new image/config/concurrency/resources with old revision. Inspect HPA metric/request math, quota, node allocatable and rollout surge. If old capacity is safe, pause or roll back through the Deployment. Verify observed generation, old revision endpoints and normal requests. Reproduce bounded memory behavior, correct code/resources, reserve surge headroom and add revision-specific rollout guards before retry.
foundation: Rollout, resource enforcement, placement, readiness and autoscaling are interacting loops with separate evidence.
reasoningSteps: Declare impact and freeze concurrent change.
Compare resource/config delta with old revision.
Inspect HPA denominator and placement capacity.
Pause or rollback at owner level.
seniorAnswer: I protect old capacity, avoid random Pod deletion and treat HPA desired replicas as intent rather than capacity. I correlate OOM and readiness inside bound new Pods while separately diagnosing Pending replicas. Recovery is a policy-driven owner rollback, proven by revision-aware endpoint and user evidence; prevention covers memory behavior, request/limit calibration, surge capacity and rollout abort signals.
weakAnswer: Raise memory limits, maxReplicas and progressDeadlineSeconds.
whyWeak: It changes three controls without proving cause, can exhaust nodes and hides a bad revision.
